summary: Marin County fire lookout on Barnabe Mountain in Samuel P. Taylor State Park. Newspapers date its build to 1938-40 (NHLR says 1935); rebuilt 1975; county says it is staffed seasonally.

facts.design: 14x14 ft flattop cab on a two-story tower (NHLR); the 1935 structure was replaced in 1975

staffing.status: seasonal, volunteer lookout program, June to late November
staffing.as_of: post dated 28 Sep, year not shown (NextDoor)

access.note: Administered by the Marin County Fire Department as an active county lookout, inside Samuel P. Taylor State Park. No source read says the tower is open to visitors or climbing. The rental page's park description gives trails and fire roads to the top of Mount Barnabe.

visit.trail_note: State park trails and fire roads reach the top of Mount Barnabe; the lookout is an active county fire facility.

events.note: NHLR and a rental page reprinting its text say the first structure was placed into service in 1935 as a 14x14 flattop on a two-story tower. The 1938-40 newspapers conflict with this date
Dickson family donated the summit and a right-of-way for a two-mile service road to the Tamalpais Forest Fire District; grading of the road began in December 1938
Mill Valley Record (May 1939) said the new Dickson Lookout station was expected to be fully complete by June 1, and that a lookout had already moved in
San Anselmo Herald (May 30, 1940) called the lookout newly constructed and set its dedication for June 9
Tamalpais Forest Fire District gave the land to the county
Newspaper reported a fireman found dead at the foot of a stairway at the lookout while making repairs before the season opened (name omitted here)
NHLR says the 1935 structure was replaced (rebuilt) in 1975
Registered July 31, 2005, as US 643, CA 76; nominated by Marin County Fire
County supervisors agreed to rededicate the lookout as the Dickson Fire Lookout at the Dickson family's request

corrections.proposed: 1938-39 construction, June 1940 dedication; 1935 kept only as NHLR's conflicting date
corrections.why: Two Forest Lookouts newspaper transcripts (Dec 1938 construction start, May 1939 near-complete station, May 1940 dedication notice) do not fit an 1935 start. The NHLR date is not corroborated by any source read. The editor should confirm before the record changes.
NHLR and the rental page quoting it describe a two-story tower. No source read says the lookout has three stories.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR and the rental page say the first structure was placed into service in 1935. Newspaper transcripts show construction in late 1938 and 1939 and a dedication in June 1940. The story reports both dates and does not choose one. See corrections.
The NHLR gives 1,460 ft (445 m), which matches the record. Newspapers quoted by Forest Lookouts give 1,470 ft (1938) and 1,477 ft (1940) for Barnabe Peak.

notes_for_editor: The build date is the main open question: NHLR says 1935, and newspapers describe 1938-40 construction. The record's height_m of 23.0 is not supported by any source read, so it was left out of facts. The record's kind three_story conflicts with the NHLR's two-story tower. A 1950 Daily Independent Journal item in the Forest Lookouts list reports a dedication on June 8, 1950, probably a retrospective column; unresolved and not used. The rental listing is cited only for its repeat of the 1935 and 1975 dates; the story does not say the lookout is rented out. The NextDoor post shows only '28 Sep' with no year. The 1961 death is reported without the name. The ffla-ccwr and firelookout.org pages were not read.
